acceptance.item: Review 1 (major): the basis is sorted by number, not by text. The full numeric decreasing order is checked over the 24 rows of D4 node 2 and the 240 of E8 node 8. The rows are checked to be the roots a = C p of the golden positive_roots. Row 5 of D4 node 2, which the oracle gives as (1,-1,1,1), is computed in the test as the sum of the simple roots, and row 8 as -alpha_2, both from C; the row indices come from lie_games, noted in a comment. The mutant that sorts by joined text: survived before, killed after (3 failed).
acceptance.test: p5-minuscule.test.ts > the basis is in numeric order where 2 and -2 occur, not in the order of the text (trap 2)

acceptance.item: Review 2: serre-f is built from F. Two cases use different E and F lists: in one serre-e fails and serre-f holds, in the other the reverse. The mutants 'serre-f computed with E' and 'serre-f starts from E[j]' survived before and are killed after, as are their serre-e mirrors.
acceptance.test: p5-rep-units.test.ts > the Serre exponent is 1 - C[i][j]... > serre-e is built from E alone and serre-f from F alone

acceptance.item: Review 3: the default cap is pinned. A13 node 5 (C(14,5) = 2002 positions) is null with the default cap and built at cap 2002; B32 node 2 (1984 positions) is built by default. A comment says an orbit of exactly 2000 needs a board of 1000 nodes (B1000, C1000, D1000 node 1), so the boundary is covered by the cap = orbit size cases. The mutant default 2010 survived before and is killed after; 2002, 1983 and 1900 are also killed.
acceptance.test: p5-rep-units.test.ts > cap > the default cap is pinned next to CAPS.repOrbit

acceptance.item: Review 4: the A1 caps 2 and 1 and the A2 cap 3 are no longer typed. They are read through the harness as types.A1.fundamental_orbit_sizes[0] and types.A2.fundamental_orbit_sizes[0].
acceptance.test: p5-rep-units.test.ts > cap > null when the orbit...; p5-guards.test.ts > argument errors > minusculeMatrices...

acceptance.item: Review 5: keys are checked the same way everywhere. spMul, spAdd, spScale and spEq (and spComm through spMul) check every key, including explicit-zero entries, and throw RangeError on a key that spKey would not write. The new tests are red on the old source and green after. The decision entry was added and two earlier entries were updated.
acceptance.test: p5-rep-units.test.ts > sparse operations > every sparse operation refuses a key that spKey would not write, in the same way (RangeError); p5-guards.test.ts > argument errors > signedMoves and chevalleySerre: a matrix key that spKey would not write

openQuestions: orbitSize(boardFromName('B32'), omega_2) throws EngineOverflow on the SafeInt board because it forms |W(B32)| before dividing. This is guarded behaviour and not a bug of phase 5. I noticed it while writing the cap test and left that one cross-check out (it stays for A13).
handoff: All five review findings are fixed and each review mutant is shown to die: the 5 survivors of the review are now killed (47 of 49 mutants in all). The two that survive are an equivalent mutant (cap < 0: orbit throws RangeError on cap 0 itself) and a default of 2001, which no board of fewer than 1000 nodes can tell apart from 2000. The only source change is in rep.ts: spAdd, spScale and spEq now refuse malformed keys as spMul did, so signedMoves and chevalleySerre do too.
